selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: How does the passage begin religiously?
questions.answer: It opens with praising Allah, asking Him for help, and sending blessings and peace upon Prophet Muhammad, his family, and his companions.

questions.question: What does the speaker say the listener had asked for?
questions.answer: He had asked for some brief advice.

questions.question: In what form does the speaker say the advice will be given?
questions.answer: It will be given through eight short stories built as comparisons connected to military life.

questions.question: Why does the speaker choose military-style comparisons?
questions.answer: Because the person being addressed is a soldier.

questions.question: Who does the speaker say needs this advice most?
questions.answer: He says his own self needs it more than anyone else.

questions.question: What earlier work of the speaker is mentioned?
questions.answer: He mentions that he had previously addressed his own self with eight “Words” drawn from eight Qur’anic verses that benefited him.

questions.question: How will the present advice differ from that earlier treatment?
questions.answer: This time it will be shorter and expressed in plain, everyday language.

questions.question: Who is invited to benefit from the advice besides the direct listener?
questions.answer: Anyone who wants may listen along and benefit too.

questions.question: Who may listen besides the one first addressed?
questions.answer: Anyone who wants to listen may join in.

questions.question: What are the main acts of worship and respect found at the opening of the passage?
questions.answer: Seeking Allah’s help, praising Him, and asking blessings and peace for the Prophet and those close to him.

questions.question: What does the speaker call the pieces of advice he is about to share?
questions.answer: He calls them truths presented in eight brief stories.

questions.question: What clue shows that the advice is adjusted to the listener’s situation?
questions.answer: The examples are shaped around military comparisons because the listener is a soldier.

questions.question: What does the speaker’s statement about his own self show about his character?
questions.answer: It shows humility and self-awareness, because he does not act as if he is above the advice.

questions.question: From where did the speaker say the earlier eight teachings were inspired?
questions.answer: They were inspired by eight verses from the Qur’an.

questions.question: What benefit had the speaker gained from those Qur’anic verses?
questions.answer: He had personally benefited from them.

questions.question: Why might the speaker choose ordinary language here?
questions.answer: So the advice will be easier to understand and more practical for the listener and others.

questions.question: What invitation at the end of the passage broadens the audience?
questions.answer: The speaker says that anyone who wishes may listen together with him.

questions.question: What does the closing invitation teach about sharing beneficial knowledge?
questions.answer: Beneficial guidance should stay open to all who sincerely want to hear it.

questions.question: To whom is the advice directly addressed in the passage?
questions.answer: It is directly addressed to a brother who asked for advice.

questions.question: What does the word “few” suggest about the advice requested?
questions.answer: It suggests the listener wanted something brief, not a long lecture.

questions.question: How many short stories are mentioned?
questions.answer: Eight.

questions.question: What is the relationship between the short stories and the truths being taught?
questions.answer: The stories are the way the truths will be explained and delivered.

questions.question: Why does the speaker mention his own inner self in this introduction?
questions.answer: To show that the advice applies to him too and is not only for someone else.

questions.question: What can we infer from the speaker’s earlier long address to his own self?
questions.answer: We can infer that he has already reflected deeply on these lessons before sharing them now.
